A1.justification: Both 23-page PDFs describe FedRot-LoRA and contain matching main sections and Appendices A–B. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original GLUE, GSM8K, and HumanEval experiments in Section 5, together with ablations and empirical alignment diagnostics in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results in Section 5 and the experimental analyses in Appendix B. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged from v2.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same alternating factor alignment, Procrustes rotations, soft rotation, local training, and aggregation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five GLUE tasks, GSM8K, and HumanEval with CodeSearchNet training. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3–5 retain FedIT, FlexLoRA, FFA-LoRA, and RoLoRA as comparators. The comparator sets in the aggregation-error and ablation experiments, including Tables 6 and 9–11, also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B.2 preserve the same models, data partitions, client counts, ranks, validation procedures, training budgets, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The rank and heterogeneity analyses, alignment ablations, rotation-strength sensitivity, reference-selection tests, and empirical checks of theoretical assumptions are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix B.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds and the same mean and standard-deviation reporting practices in Section 5 and Appendix B.2. No statistical procedure or uncertainty disclosure changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and Appendix B. For example, Table 5 retains FedRot-LoRA's HumanEval pass@1 of 0.4088 ± 0.012 and GSM8K accuracy of 0.4437 ± 0.009.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, convergence and aggregation-error bounds, and proofs in Section 4 and Appendix A are identical. The mathematical derivations in Appendix B also remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about rotational misalignment, tighter error bounds, communication cost, and empirical advantages.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning heterogeneity, noisy references, excessive alignment, and conservative theoretical conditions remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: The framework, GPU hardware, hyperparameters, experimental instructions, and code-access information remain unchanged in Section 5.1, Appendix B, and the abstract.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged. Matching reference entries across the shifted page breaks establishes that no citation or research-positioning change occurred.

P1.justification: v3 adds an Acknowledgements heading and one sentence crediting NSF Grant 2148224 after the conclusion. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the research prose and existing section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement changes spacing and placement around Table 6 and the conclusion on page 9, and reflows the impact statement and references on pages 9–11. Figure and table contents, structures, and numbering are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds funding attribution on page 9, but the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive explanations—including both appendices—are unchanged. The acknowledgement and minor layout reflow do not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
